title: Spatial temperature controls reduced the Pacific warm-cold volume slope contrast in 1980-2024 fits
abstract: We tested whether spatial surface temperature controls change the warm-minus-cold slope contrast for six-month equatorial Pacific warm water volume change. We used frozen NOAA GODAS and ERSSTv5 data with 531 monthly starts in 1980-2024. Adding Nino 3 minus Nino 4 and its three-month change moved the contrast from -1.171 to -0.355 in units of 10^14 cubic metres per degree C. The paired change was +0.816, with conditional 95% three-year block limits of +0.352 to +1.174. The adjusted contrast had limits of -0.851 to +0.055. Five-year blocks and nonlinear spatial controls retained attenuation. An alternate coastal contrast and omission of major event years retained negative adjusted contrasts. Thus spatial controls account statistically for part of the fitted contrast, but do not establish a full physical explanation. Few ENSO cycles, revised products, model choices and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, provenance, a numerical audit and a figure are included. Source records stay outside the package.
